about: The game utkarsh wants, written as things we can measure. Each pillar quotes what he asked for, each metric says how it is measured and what 'good' is. npm run eval scores every metric 0..1 between its floor and its target, a pillar is the weighted mean of its metrics, and the vision score is the weighted mean of the pillars. Metrics that can't be measured in this run (no browser, no judge, no playtest yet) are listed as not measured and left out of the mean, so a partial score says so.
rules: The north star is utkarsh's own rating after playing (pillar 'you'). No automatic number overrides it: if the score went up and he says it got worse, the eval is wrong and gets fixed first.

Hill-climb one pillar at a time: pick the pillar with the biggest weight x gap, change the game, run npm run eval, keep the change only if that pillar went up and no other pillar fell by more than 3 points. npm run verify must still pass.
More words is not more game. Reading load and narration are scored against you, so adding dialogue can lower the score.

A new low-level game (a chase variant, kabaddi, the window escape, a chant) must emit engine cues named action:<game>:start, action:<game>:win and action:<game>:fail, and be listed by affordances(s), or the eval can't see it.
